$schema_note: Canonical evidence vocabulary for ComplianceGuard scoring. Evidence is framework-agnostic by TYPE; a control's required_evidence list (shared/frameworks/*_controls.yaml) determines which types satisfy it. 'legacy_aliases' are the old Python-map evidence_type values that translate to this canonical type (see canonical_evidence.py translate_evidence_types).

canonical_types.description: Access/authentication log records (e.g., login activity, access attempts).
Audit records/reports: review results, audit trail evidence, independent assessment artifacts.
Encryption configuration and policy evidence (at-rest/in-transit encryption, key management).
System/event/audit log evidence from the endpoint or cloud.
Firewall state and rule configuration evidence.
Security configuration/policy evidence from the endpoint (password policy, audit policy, hardening).
System/OS configuration evidence (services, installed software, file permissions, system info).
User account/provisioning evidence (account inventory, MFA enforcement, access reviews).

note: legacy_aliases are translation inputs only: web-mode evidence stored under the old Python vocabulary is translated to its canonical type before scoring. Types with no alias (access_logs, backup_logs) can only be satisfied by manual uploads today.

inert_mappings.reason: HIPAA Security Rule controls consume network_configs / encryption_policies / event_logs for transmission security (164.312.e.2.i-ii); no HIPAA control lists firewall_configs in required_evidence. A legacy 'firewall' item therefore does not affect HIPAA scoring. Intentional — not a gap to force by adding arbitrary evidence requirements.

GDPR controls in the canonical definitions do not list training_records in required_evidence (training maps to Art.32/39 via security_policies in practice). A legacy 'training_records' item therefore does not affect GDPR scoring. If product wants training records to influence GDPR, the GDPR control definitions must be updated deliberately — not via translation.
